newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan agency appeals for aid, criticises U.N.
newsitem.headline: Afghan agency appeals for aid, criticises U.N.

text.p: The Afghan Red Crescent Society appealed for 25,000 tonnes of food aid on Saturday and said outside relief agencies were failing to help many families in need.
"According to our statistics there are 500,000 families in Afghanistan who need to be given free foodstuffs and relief items," Red Crescent head Sayed Ahmed Gafoori told a news conference.
"As an emergency step, the ARCS needs 25,000 tonnes of food items for the families who are in need of help."

Gafoori told reporters the United Nations and international aid organisations were failing to help Afghans uprooted from the Shomali Valley north of Kabul and by fighting in the north-western province of Badghis.
"Neither the UN nor charitable institutions have helped the people of Shomali. Their intention of helping the people after they have gone back to their villages is unacceptable." he said.

The United Nations estimates that the purist Islamic Taleban have forced more than 140,000 people to leave their homes in the Shomali Valley to Kabul as a security measure, and that a further 36,000 have been displaced by fighting in Badghis.
Many of the displaced from Shomali are living in schools and other public buildings in Kabul. The Taleban have not allowed them to return to their homes.
Rupert Colville of the United Nations told Reuters that the U.N. had helped some of the displaced, but that they were hoping that the Taleban would allow people to return to the Shomali Valley.
"Some of the displaced people have been helped, and others have been brought into existing programmes that help vulnerable groups." Colville said
"We are still hoping for a reversal of the policy of not allowing people to return to their homes." he said.
The United Nations refugee agency said on Tuesday that 800 people uprooted from the Shomali Valley had been arriving in Kabul each day for three weeks.
Spokeswoman Pam O'Toole also told a news conference in Geneva that the effects of the displacement would be felt beyond those who had been displaced.
She said that the Shomali valley was an important source of food for Kabul, and that this is the spring planting season.
"At this time of year, the population should be planting their crops and pruning their fruit trees, not themselves struggling for food." she said.
The Red Crescent's Gafoori also said that the U.N. was claiming to have assisted people without achieving anything on the ground.
"The U.N. is always publicising how much they help, but in practical terms they have not achieved much." said Gafoori.
